ai.description: This snake reaches 25–30 cm. It is dark brown above with yellow lateral spots and a pale belly. It features a truncated, shield-like tail and a pointed snout. Family: Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis shorttii* is best distinguished by its unique, heavily keeled, and strongly bicarinate scales on the terminal tail shield, which form a distinct, rough disc.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis shorttii* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Shevaroy Hills in the Eastern Ghats, typically at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis shorttii* is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending its time burrowing through moist soil to forage for earthworms and other soft-bodied invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis shorttii* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis shorttii* is endemic to the Shevaroy Hills in the Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
